comment: Landale (hip) won't play Sunday against the Pistons.
detail: This will be Landale's fourth consecutive game on the inactive list. His next chance to play will come Friday in Boston.

comment: Newell underwent surgery Tuesday for a plantar plate tear in his left great toe, and he will be re-evaluated in approximately four months, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
detail: Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

comment: McCollum (calf) will miss at least four weeks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.
detail: The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.

comment: Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
detail: The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

comment: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
detail: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

comment: Robinson (illness) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Golden State, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
detail: Robinson will miss both halves of this back-to-back set due to an illness. The big man's next opportunity to play will come Tuesday at Washington. Luka Garza will likely see increased minutes in Robinson's stead.

comment: George (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Golden State, Justin Turpin of WEEI.com reports.
detail: George will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. With the veteran forward sidelined, Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez and Sam Hauser could all see increased burn. George will likely return for Tuesday's game at Washington.

comment: Nelson (ankle) is probable for Monday's game against the Timberwolves.
detail: Nelson looks poised to come off the inactive list due to a sprained right ankle. However, his presence is not likely to affect Brooklyn's rotation.

comment: Traore (hamstring) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Timberwolves.
detail: Traore started the previous three games for Brooklyn, but he was forced to leave Friday's 113-111 loss to Orlando early due to a right hamstring strain. That same injury will force the second-year guard to miss his second contest of 2026-27. Egor Demin could return to the starting lineup with Traore sidelined.

comment: Allen (concussion) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
detail: Allen is set to miss a third consecutive contest due to a concussion. Sion James will continue to start while Royce O'Neale should get more minutes off the bench.

comment: Miller is probable for Monday's game against the Grizzlies due to a right knee contusion.
detail: Miller is dealing with a right knee bone bruise, but he is expected to suit up Monday. In three games since returning from a groin injury, Miller has averaged 17.3 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.7 assists in 29.7 minutes per contest.

comment: Williams (hamstring) won't play Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
detail: Williams will miss a second consecutive game due to right hamstring injury management. Royce O'Neale and Tidjane Salaun should continue to see more minutes off the bench for Charlotte.

comment: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
detail: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

comment: Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
detail: Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

comment: Claxton (illness) won't play in Sunday's game against the Nuggets.
detail: Claxton will miss Sunday's contest due to an illness. He started Friday's 98-94 loss to the Wizards with Jalen Smith (illness) sidelined, but the latter is expected to return versus Denver. Zach Collins and Noa Essengue should get a bump in opportunities with Claxton out.

comment: Powell has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated later this week.
detail: Powell sustained the hamstring injury in Friday's loss to the Wizards and is now set to miss at least the next two contests. With the veteran swingman on the shelf, Isaac Okoro, Buddy Hield, Tre Jones and Patrick Williams are all candidates for increased playing time.

comment: Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

comment: Tyson (ankle) is probable for Monday's game against the Bulls.
detail: Tyson has missed the last three games due to right ankle injury management. An upgrade to probable is a good sign, but we'll need to get confirmation from Cleveland prior to tipoff in Chicago. If he does indeed suit up, Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas could all see their minutes dip.

comment: Tomlin (back) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
detail: Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

comment: Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days.
detail: Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

comment: Washington (illness) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jazz.
detail: Washington is under the weather and will remain on the inactive list for a second consecutive contest. His next chance to play will come Tuesday at Denver. Zaccharie Risacher, Morez Johnson and Naji Marshall are candidates for increased burn in Washington's absence.

comment: Lawal (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jazz.
detail: Lawal will miss a third consecutive game due to a right groin strain. His absence won't have much of an impact on the Mavericks' rotation. Lawal's next chance to suit up will come Tuesday against Denver.

comment: Head coach Dusty May said Friday that Lively (foot) is moving well and progressing in his recovery, and the big man told May he's "close" to returning, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
detail: Lively hasn't seen game action since Nov. 21, 2025, and he remains without a firm timetable to return after undergoing right foot surgery last December. However, this update suggests that the big man is trending in the right direction.

comment: De Larrea (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
detail: De Larrea has only played four games during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been any indication of when he will be cleared to return, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

comment: Biberovic (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
detail: Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and the fact that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Biberovic should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

comment: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
detail: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

comment: Okorie (oblique) is out for Sunday's game in Atlanta.
detail: This will be Okorie's second straight game on the inactive list due to injury. His next chance to play will come Tuesday in Orlando.

comment: Prince (knee) underwent surgery to address lingering issues and has no timeline for a return, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
detail: With Detroit still without a return timetable for Prince after right knee surgery, he appears set for an extended absence well beyond Friday's tilt against Toronto. Prince hasn't been a significant part of the Pistons' rotation this season, so his continued absence is unlikely to create a major fantasy ripple effect.

comment: Robinson will be re-evaluated in one week due to a left quadriceps strain, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
detail: Robinson has gotten off to a strong start this season, though he's now expected to miss at least the next week after appearing in each of Detroit's first 12 regular-season games. The sharpshooter is averaging 17.4 points in 30.5 minutes per contest, and his absence will open up additional minutes for Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green.

comment: Duren (hamstring) has begun on-court activity and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
detail: Duren is progressing in his rehab after suffering a right hamstring strain Oct. 23, though he'll remain on the inactive list for at least the next two weeks while ramping up toward a return to game action. Paul Reed should continue to play a sizable role in Duren's stead.

comment: Williams (hamstring) is out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
detail: Williams recently progressed to on-court work, but he will remain on the inactive list for Sunday's game. His next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Kings.

comment: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

comment: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
detail: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

comment: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
detail: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

comment: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
detail: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

comment: McConnell (hamstring) is listed as out for Sunday's game in New York.
detail: McConnell missed the Pacers' first nine games of the 2026-27 campaign because of a right hamstring issue. However, he exited Friday's 128-119 loss to the Cavaliers due to left hamstring soreness. McConnell will have another opportunity to play Monday versus Oklahoma City, but for now, he should be considered day-to-day. In the meantime, Quenton Jackson is in line for more minutes behind Andrew Nembhard.

comment: Haliburton (hamstring) is expected to miss at least two more weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: Haliburton hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a left hamstring strain, and the Pacers won't rush him back. With the star floor general unlikely to return until mid-December at the earliest, Quenton Jackson and T.J. McConnell are candidates for increased playing time, while Andrew Nembhard figures to continue seeing increased playmaking duties.

comment: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
detail: The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

comment: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
detail: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

comment: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
detail: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

comment: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
detail: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

comment: Reaves (heel) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Jazz, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
detail: Reaves will miss a fifth consecutive game due to a bruised left heel. His next chance to suit up will come against the Spurs on Friday. Quentin Grimes should remain in the starting lineup versus Utah, while Collin Sexton and Cameron Carr are likely to see additional minutes off the Lakers' bench.

comment: Grant was diagnosed with a grade 1 left calf strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
detail: Grant suffered the injury during Thursday's 126-98 victory over Golden State. He will now be sidelined for at least two weeks, with the team expected to provide an update on his condition at that time. While Grant is on the shelf, Taylor Hendricks and Kris Murray are candidates for more minutes.

comment: Boozer (ankle) won't play Monday's game against the Hornets.
detail: Boozer will miss a second straight outing due to a sprained right ankle. Jahmai Mashack got the start during Saturday's 104-95 loss to Minnesota, but we'll have to wait and see if Memphis opts to switch things up versus Charlotte. With Boozer sidelined, Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks will continue earning extra minutes.

comment: Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months.
detail: Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

comment: Pippen (back) is progressing in his recovery but is still considered week-to-week.
detail: Pippen hasn't played since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a firm timetable to return.  Cam Spencer and Javon Small will likely continue seeing increased playing time in Pippen's absence.

comment: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

comment: Antetokounmpo (groin) won't play in Sunday's game against Oklahoma City, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
detail: Antetokounmpo is dealing with a groin injury. He was initially listed as questionable, though he has since been ruled out, marking his first absence of the year. His next opportunity to suit up will come Wednesday against Philadelphia. In the meantime, Bobby Portis and Andrew Wiggins are candidates to fill the void in the starting lineup.

comment: Dieng (finger) is questionable for Monday's game against the Raptors.
detail: Dieng has missed the last four games while recovering from a procedure to repair a fractured left finger. He reportedly underwent surgery Nov. 16, so his questionable status is somewhat shocking considering it's only been one week. Still, Milwaukee will provide another update prior to tip.

comment: Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks.
detail: Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

comment: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
detail: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

comment: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
detail: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

comment: Murphy (knees) is listed as probable for Monday's game against the Suns.
detail: Murphy has missed seven of New Orleans' past eight games due to bilateral patellar tendinopathy, though he's expected to suit up Monday. The 26-year-old swingman logged 29 minutes off the bench in Friday's loss to the Thunder, marking his return after a six-game stint on the inactive list. He could remain restricted if he's cleared to play Monday.

comment: McGowens (elbow) is listed as probable for Monday's game against Phoenix.
detail: McGowens has missed the Pelicans' last six games due to a left elbow infection, but it's an encouraging sign to see him listed as probable to return Monday. In seven regular-season outings, he's averaged 3.7 points and 1.1 steals in 10.6 minutes per game.

comment: Williamson (thigh) is probable for Monday's game against Phoenix.
detail: Williamson sat out Saturday's 114-91 loss to San Antonio due to a left thigh contusion, but it sounds like he's trending in the right direction for Monday. His return would likely shift Derik Queen back to the bench.

comment: Watford (ankle) is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
detail: Watford can be considered week-to-week at this point until the Pelicans offer an update on his recovery. He hasn't played since Nov. 8 and is averaging just 7.2 points and 3.5 boards per game in his six appearances off the bench.

comment: Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
detail: Mathurin will miss a fourth straight contest due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which tends to be a lingering injury. Jordan Poole should remain in the backcourt rotation for the undermanned Pelicans moving forward, while Mathurin can be deemed week-to-week.

comment: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
detail: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

comment: McBride (abdomen) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Pacers.
detail: McBride will miss his first outing of the 2026-27 campaign due to left adductor tightness. Tyler Kolek and Jose Alvarado should absorb the majority of the vacated minutes off the Knicks' bench.

comment: Anunoby (calf) won't play Sunday against the Pacers.
detail: Anunoby will miss a second straight game due to left calf tightness. Landry Shamet got the start in Saturday's 97-96 win over Portland, so fantasy managers should expect the same versus Indiana. Anunoby's next chance to suit up will come against the Cavaliers on Wednesday.

comment: Clarkson (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Indiana.
detail: Clarkson will miss a third consecutive game due to plantar fasciitis in his right foot. In his absence, Tyler Kolek and Jose Alvarado should see an uptick in playing time off the Knicks' bench. Clarkson's next chance to suit up will come Wednesday against Cleveland.

comment: Mara (shin) is listed as out for Sunday's game versus Miami.
detail: Mara is the latest Thunder player to be added to the injury report. With Jaylin Williams (back), Jalen Williams (leg) and Chet Holmgren (knee) also sidelined, more minutes should be available for Kenrich Williams and Micah Peavy.

comment: Gilgeous-Alexander (back/neck) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Heat.
detail: Gilgeous-Alexander will miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign. His next opportunity to suit up will come Monday against the Pacers. Nikola Topic (hip), Alex Caruso (hip) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) are also unavailable, so Bennett Stirtz, Kenrich Williams and Nique Clifford are candidates for more minutes, with one of those players potentially moving into the starting lineup.

comment: Topic (hip) is listed as out for Sunday's game versus the Heat.
detail: Topic has appeared in only three games for Oklahoma City this season. He will now miss a second consecutive contest due to a hip injury, with his next opportunity to play coming Monday versus the Pacers. Considering Topic has averaged just 11.3 minutes per outing, his absence won't have much of an effect on the rotation, though he might have seen more action if Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (back/neck), who is questionable, can't suit up.

comment: Williams (back) is listed as out for Sunday's game against Miami.
detail: Williams missed seven consecutive contests due to back spasms. He has since appeared in the Thunder's last two games. However, the 24-year-old won't suit up Sunday against the Heat, the first game of a back-to-back for Oklahoma City. Without Williams on the floor, Aday Mara, Kenrich Williams and Micah Peavy could see more minutes.

comment: Caruso (hip) won't play Sunday against the Heat.
detail: Sunday will mark Caruso's second straight game on the sidelines, but maybe he'll be able to get back out there for Monday's meeting in Indiana. Bennett Stirtz and Nique Clifford will help pick up the slack in Caruso's absence.

comment: Sorber underwent an arthroscopic knee procedure Tuesday to address inflammation at the patellofemoral joint in his right knee, and he's expected to return to on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, Steve McGehee of News 9 Oklahoma City reports.
detail: Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

comment: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
detail: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

comment: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
detail: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

comment: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
detail: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

comment: Isaac (knee) is out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
detail: Isaac continues to deal with a knee injury that has kept him out of action for the entire 2026-27 season. He should continue to be considered week to week until the Magic offer an update on his recovery process.

comment: Head coach Sean Sweeney said Wednesday that Nelson (ankle) has been doing "some on-court stuff," though Sweeney added that the work has been "minimal," Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
detail: Nelson underwent surgery this offseason to repair a fractured left ankle. It's encouraging to hear that he's made some progress, but the two-way player can still be considered week-to-week moving forward.

comment: Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
detail: Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

comment: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

comment: Bona (back) is listed as probable for Monday's game against the Trail Blazers.
detail: Bona is on track to return after missing the last eight regular-season games. It's unclear if he will be limited in his first game back, though he is expected to reclaim his spot as the No. 2 center on the roster behind Joel Embiid.

comment: Brown (hamstring) is listed as probable for Monday's game versus Portland.
detail: Brown has a left hamstring strain, though it appears he will suit up after missing only two games. It's unclear if he will see limited action in his first game back from the brief layoff. However, Brown's return would mean Kentavious Caldwell-Pope would revert to a reserve role.

comment: Wade (hamstring) is listed as probable for Monday's game against Portland.
detail: Wade is expected to return from a two-game absence due to a left hamstring injury. His return would leave fewer minutes available for guys like Jabari Walker and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope.

comment: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
detail: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

comment: Dunn (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Pelicans.
detail: Dunn exited Friday's win over Utah early due to right quad soreness, and despite practicing in full Sunday, he's still questionable to suit up versus New Orleans.

comment: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

comment: Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Knicks.
detail: Youngblood has been on the shelf since Nov. 10 due to a right heel bone bruise. Until Portland signals otherwise, Youngblood can be considered out indefinitely moving forward.

comment: Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
detail: Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

comment: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
detail: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

comment: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
detail: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

comment: Raynaud (knee) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Suns.
detail: Raynaud continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff, suggesting he's still not close. He should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

comment: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
detail: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

comment: Wembanyama (back) is questionable for Monday's game against the Kings, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
detail: Wembanyama is dealing with lower-back tightness, leaving his status for Monday's road tilt up in the air. If he's unable to play, Luke Kornet would likely replace Wembanyama in the starting lineup, while Carter Bryant, Keldon Johnson and rookie Tarris Reed Jr. could all see a bump in minutes off the Spurs' bench.

comment: Fox is questionable for Monday's game against the Kings due to a right shin contusion, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
detail: Fox could miss Monday's game due to a shin injury he likely picked up during Saturday's game against the Pelicans. With Dylan Harper (hip) out and Jordan McLaughlin (shoulder) questionable, the Spurs could be thin at the lead guard position, leaving more ball-handling responsibilities for Stephon Castle.

comment: McLaughlin (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Kings.
detail: McLaughlin may miss his seventh game of the year. With De'Aaron Fox (shin) also questionable and Dylan Harper (hip) already sidelined, McLaughlin would be in line to receive extra minutes if he manages to suit up. However, if he's not available versus Sacramento, David Jones Garcia could see significantly more work than usual.

comment: Harper (hip) is expected to miss two to three weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
detail: Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain, and San Antonio is now set to be without one of its regular guards for an extended stretch. His absence creates more backcourt minutes for the Spurs, likely most prominently for Justin Champagnie while the team waits for Tobias Harris (calf) to make his season debut. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle should see extra ball-handling duties as well.

comment: Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio.
detail: Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

comment: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
detail: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

comment: Murray-Boyles (concussion) is listed as probable for Monday's game against Milwaukee, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
detail: Murray-Boyles exited Wednesday's game versus the Wizards and didn't suit up for Friday's 105-102 win over the Pistons. It appears a one-game absence will be all that is needed for the 21-year-old, though it's unclear if he will reclaim his spot in the starting lineup over Allen Graves.

comment: Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bucks, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
detail: Bittle continues to work his way back from a fractured right foot, as he's yet to make his 2026-27 season debut. He remains week-to-week until Toronto provides a definitive update.

comment: Leonard (knee) could return in the next few weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
detail: This was the expectation after the Raptors ruled out the star forward Tuesday for at least one more week. Collin Murray-Boyles should continue to handle a larger role once he passes the concussion protocol, and Ja'Kobe Walter should remain a starter for the time being.

comment: Barrett has been diagnosed with a right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
detail: Based on his re-evaluation timeline, Barrett likely won't return to game action until mid-December at the earliest. Jamison Battle, Allen Graves and Jamal Shead are candidates for increased playing time in Barrett's absence, especially while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is also sidelined.

comment: Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Mavericks, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
detail: Hayes will not return Sunday due to a left knee injury. Mo Bamba will soak up most of Hayes' vacated minutes, while Brice Sensabaugh and Tony Bradley could see additional opportunities.

comment: Nurkic (foot) has been cleared for on-court work and will be re-evaluated in one week.
detail: Nurkic continues to make progress in his recovery from a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe on his right foot, and getting cleared for on-court work is a big step in his rehab. There are still a few steps he'll need to clear before he makes his return to the floor, but once he's able to get through full-contact, 5-on-5 work, we'll know he's close.

comment: Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
detail: Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

comment: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
detail: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

comment: Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Memphis.
detail: Vukcevic has yet to make his season debut due to a left hip injury. He can be considered week-to-week until the Wizards offer an update on his progress.

comment: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
detail: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

comment: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
detail: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

comment: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
detail: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.
